doc.title: Jack DeJohnette — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: The history of drumming on "Last Chance Stomp"
summary: He recalls changing his sound across eras on The Cosmic Chicken.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Early drum kits and the gear drummers used

blocks.x: Well, you referenced “four on the floor,” so being cognizant of the historical evolution of jazz drumming… Which is not something new because I’m looking back at The Cosmic Chicken, where you did a selection called, “Last Chance Stomp,” where you did an abridged history of jazz drumming.
It was interesting because I changed the sound as I changed eras.

You show the stylistic evolution but also show (that) the recording quality/fidelity evolves, too. I just say that to underscore the fact that you know the history of the drum set and when you say “four on the floor” that definitely signals that. As we move ahead in 2005 you launch three projects. The Latin Project, The Jack
DeJohnette Quartet and then the Beyond Trio, so if you want to talk about them…
